claims.text: Introducing rare-earth elements such as Nd or Dy into a magnetic high-entropy alloy enhances its magnetic anisotropy.
Enhanced magnetic anisotropy caused by rare-earth addition increases the coercive field.
A rare-earth-containing alloy will have a higher coercive field than a matched alloy without rare-earth elements.
The predicted coercivity increase applies to as-cast or annealed magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The predicted effect should occur at room temperature under a variable applied magnetic field.
The hypothesis is restricted to a composition range in which rare-earth addition does not significantly change the microstructure.
The hypothesis is restricted to a composition range in which rare-earth addition does not significantly change other magnetic properties.
An increase of less than 10% in coercive field relative to the matched baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary requires no significant change in other magnetic properties, while the proposed mechanism requires a significant enhancement of magnetic anisotropy, itself a magnetic property. The intended exemption of anisotropy is not stated.
